# Webb’s Path from Deployment to Routine Science

The James Webb Space Telescope had to fold to fit inside the Ariane 5 fairing because its operational configuration was too large for the available rocket. Unfolding required more than 50 major steps and involved over 300 possible single points of failure. Any one could have diminished or crippled the mission, and Webb could not be repaired at its distance from Earth.

By its second week, the secondary mirror and both primary-mirror wings had unfolded and latched. Webb had reached its fully deployed operational configuration, and deployment had proceeded smoothly. But deployment was one stage of a longer commissioning period—not the point at which the telescope began routine science.

In the first month, the telescope and its instruments cooled for several weeks. Mirror alignment followed in months two through four, then instrument-mode calibration in months five and six. Webb began routine science operations after six months.
